packageRules.description: Test-only infrastructure ships nothing to production, so a bad version can only turn the required 'build' check red, which already blocks the merge. That makes these self-policing, so all update types automerge including majors.

Build-time only: SourceLink and reproducible-build SDKs emit nothing at runtime, so a bad version fails the build rather than reaching production. Nerdbank.GitVersioning is deliberately excluded because it determines published version numbers.

WireMock.Net is referenced only by the sample app and its tests, never by the shipped Lightr libraries, so a breaking change surfaces as a red 'build' check. Capped at minor/patch because this repo has very little behavioural test coverage, so the gate is closer to a compile check than a behavioural one.

Build-time generators for LightrClient: NSwag generates it and clio applies the OpenAPI overlay with --strict, so a bad version fails the required 'build' check. Capped at minor/patch because NSwag output is the shipped public API and a major can reshape it without breaking the build.

.NET servicing updates (runtime packages and dotnet-openapi) within the current major. A major (new target runtime, raised minimum Microsoft.Extensions.* version for consumers of the published package) stays a manual review. Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities is excluded because it is a security pin.
SDK servicing pin in global.json: a patch or minor SDK that breaks the build or tests fails the required 'build' check. A major SDK stays a manual review.
